stem: The graph shows Group A's antibody concentration $y$, in units per milliliter, $t$ weeks after a vaccine dose. Group B's concentration is modeled by $y = 70 - 5t$. If $(t, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Group B's equation, what is the value of $y$?
stimulus: An immunologist compares two groups of volunteers. Group A received a new vaccine and their antibody levels are rising. Group B has antibodies from an earlier infection, and their levels are slowly falling.

figure.caption: Group A Antibody Concentration
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 10), (2, 20), (4, 30), (6, 40), (8, 50), and (10, 60).

explanation: Only one line is drawn, so first read its equation off the graph. It crosses the y-axis at 10 and rises 10 units for every 2 weeks, so its slope is 5 and the line is $y = 5t + 10$. The solution is the point that lies on both lines, so set the two equal: $5t + 10 = 70 - 5t$. That gives $10t = 60$, so $t = 6$. Substitute to get $y = 5(6) + 10 = 40$. Check it in Group B's equation: $70 - 5(6) = 40$.

common_errors.why: Solved for t correctly but entered the week instead of the concentration the question asks for.
Read the graphed line's y-intercept, a point on only one of the two lines, instead of the point the lines share.
Took Group B's starting value, the constant in its equation, as the solution.
Added 10 to 70 instead of subtracting it: $10t = 80$, so $t = 8$ and $y = 5(8) + 10 = 50$.

stem: The graph shows the number of folktale versions $y$ recorded in Region P after $x$ months of fieldwork. In Region Q, the number of storytellers still waiting to be interviewed is modeled by $y = 16 - x$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and the equation for Region Q, what is the value of $x + y$?
stimulus: A folklore studies team is collecting versions of a regional legend. In Region P they log each new version of the tale as they find it. In Region Q they work through a fixed list of storytellers.

figure.caption: Folktale Versions Recorded in Region P
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 4), (1, 6), (2, 8), (3, 10), (4, 12), (5, 14), and (6, 16).

explanation: Read the graphed line first. It starts at 4 and goes up 2 for every month, so it is $y = 2x + 4$. Set it equal to Region Q's equation: $2x + 4 = 16 - x$. Then $3x = 12$, so $x = 4$, and $y = 2(4) + 4 = 12$. The question asks for the sum: $x + y = 4 + 12 = 16$.

common_errors.why: Found x and stopped before adding y.
Found y and stopped before adding x.
Added the two y-intercepts, 4 + 16, which are points on one line each, instead of using the crossing point.
Dropped the $-x$ on the right side and solved $2x = 12$ to get $x = 6$. Then $y = 2(6) + 4 = 16$, and the sum is 22.

stem: The graph shows Athlete A's heart rate $y$, in beats per minute, when running at a treadmill speed of $x$ kilometers per hour. Athlete B's heart rate is modeled by $y = 15x + 40$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Athlete B's equation, what is the value of $x$?
stimulus: A sports scientist records two athletes' heart rates during a treadmill test in which the speed is raised step by step.

figure.caption: Athlete A Heart Rate on Treadmill
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 60), (2, 80), (4, 100), (6, 120), (8, 140), (10, 160), and (12, 180).

explanation: From the graph, Athlete A's line starts at 60 and rises 20 beats for every 2 km/h, so its slope is 10 and the line is $y = 10x + 60$. Set it equal to Athlete B's equation: $10x + 60 = 15x + 40$. Subtract to get $20 = 5x$, so $x = 4$. Check: both equations give $y = 100$ when $x = 4$.

common_errors.why: Gave the y-coordinate of the solution, the heart rate, instead of the speed. This is the same as swapping the coordinates.
Read Athlete A's resting heart rate, the line's y-intercept, which is on only one of the lines.
Added the constants instead of subtracting them: $5x = 60 + 40 = 100$, so $x = 20$.
Read the slope as 20, the rise for one gridline, instead of 10 per km/h. Solving $20x + 60 = 15x + 40$ gives $x = -4$. A student who drops the sign enters 4, and one who also halves enters 2.

stem: The graph shows the water depth $y$, in centimeters, in Tide Pool 1 $x$ hours after a monitoring session began. The water depth in Tide Pool 2 is modeled by $y = 2x + 5$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Tide Pool 2's equation, how many minutes after the session began are the two depths equal?
stimulus: A marine biologist studying sea anemones measures the water depth in two connected tide pools. As the tide goes out, Tide Pool 1 drains into Tide Pool 2.

figure.caption: Water Depth in Tide Pool 1
figure.alt: A straight decreasing line passing through (0, 30), (2, 24), (4, 18), (6, 12), (8, 6), and (10, 0).

explanation: The graphed line starts at 30 and falls 6 cm every 2 hours, so its slope is $-3$ and the line is $y = 30 - 3x$. Set it equal to Tide Pool 2's equation: $30 - 3x = 2x + 5$. Then $25 = 5x$, so $x = 5$ hours, when both depths are 15 cm. The question asks for minutes, so convert: $5 \times 60 = 300$.

common_errors.why: Solved correctly but entered the time in hours without converting it to minutes.
Entered the shared depth, the y-coordinate, instead of the time.
Read Tide Pool 1's starting depth, the y-intercept, which lies on only one line.
Added 5 to 30 instead of subtracting it: $35 = 5x$, so $x = 7$ hours, which is 420 minutes.
Read the slope as positive, $y = 3x + 30$. Solving $3x + 30 = 2x + 5$ gives $x = -25$, and a student who drops the sign and converts gets 1500.

stem: The graph shows the height $h$, in centimeters, of the seedlings in Plot A $d$ days after planting. The seedlings in Plot B are modeled by $h = d + 20$. If $(d, h)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Plot B's equation, what is the value of $d$?
stimulus: An agronomist compares two plots of sorghum seedlings. Plot A was planted in tilled soil, and Plot B was planted in untilled soil a week earlier.

figure.caption: Plot A Seedling Height
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 4), (2, 10), (4, 16), (6, 22), (8, 28), and (10, 34).

explanation: Only one line is drawn, so first read its equation off the graph. It crosses the vertical axis at 4 and rises 6 cm every 2 days, so its slope is 3 and the line is $h = 3d + 4$. The solution is the point on both lines, so set them equal: $3d + 4 = d + 20$. Subtract $d$ and 4 from both sides to get $2d = 16$, so $d = 8$. Check: $3(8) + 4 = 28$ and $8 + 20 = 28$.

common_errors.why: Solved correctly but entered the shared height $h$ instead of the day $d$, which swaps the coordinates of the solution.
Read the graphed line's vertical intercept. That point lies on only one of the two lines.
Took the constant in Plot B's equation as the answer.
Added 4 to 20 instead of subtracting it: $2d = 24$, so $d = 12$.

stem: The graph shows the number of sea urchins $y$ per square meter on Reef P, $t$ months after sea otters returned. On Reef Q, $y = 2t + 6$. If $(t, y)$ is the solution to the system of the graphed line and Reef Q's equation, what is the value of $y$?
stimulus: Marine biologists are tracking sea urchins on two kelp reefs. On Reef P, otters are eating the urchins. On Reef Q, which has no otters, the urchins are spreading.

figure.caption: Sea Urchin Density on Reef P
figure.alt: A straight decreasing line passing through (0, 60), (3, 48), (6, 36), (9, 24), (12, 12), and (15, 0).

explanation: First get the graphed line's equation. It starts at 60 and falls 12 urchins every 3 months, so its slope is $-4$ and the line is $y = 60 - 4t$. Set the two expressions equal: $60 - 4t = 2t + 6$. Then $54 = 6t$, so $t = 9$. The question asks for $y$: $y = 2(9) + 6 = 24$. Check: $60 - 4(9) = 24$.

common_errors.why: Stopped at $t$ and entered the month instead of the urchin density the question asks for.
Read Reef P's starting value, the line's vertical intercept, which is not on Reef Q's line.
Took the constant in Reef Q's equation as the answer.
Added 6 to 60 instead of subtracting it: $6t = 66$, so $t = 11$ and $y = 2(11) + 6 = 28$.

stem: The graph shows the number of activated T cells $y$, in thousands, in Culture A, $x$ hours after an antigen is added. Culture B is modeled by $y = 5x - 12$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system made up of the graphed line and Culture B's equation, what is the value of $x$?
stimulus: An immunology lab adds the same antigen to two T-cell cultures. Culture B starts with fewer activated cells but responds faster.

figure.caption: Culture A Activated T Cells
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 8), (4, 20), (8, 32), and (12, 44).

explanation: Read the graphed line's equation first. It crosses the vertical axis at 8 and rises 12 thousand cells every 4 hours, so its slope is 3 and the line is $y = 3x + 8$. Set the two equal: $3x + 8 = 5x - 12$. Subtract $3x$ and add 12 to get $20 = 2x$, so $x = 10$. Check: $3(10) + 8 = 38$ and $5(10) - 12 = 38$.

common_errors.why: Entered the shared cell count $y$ instead of the time $x$, which swaps the coordinates.
Read Culture A's vertical intercept, a point on only the graphed line.
Combined $-12$ and $8$ as $-4$ instead of $-20$: $-2x = -4$, so $x = 2$.

stem: The graph shows the number of new flu cases $y$ reported per day in County A, $x$ weeks after a vaccine drive began. In County B, $y = 3x + 42$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system of the graphed line and County B's equation, what is the value of $y$?
stimulus: A public health office compares daily flu reports from two counties. County A held a vaccine drive, and County B did not.

figure.caption: County A Daily Flu Cases
figure.alt: A straight decreasing line passing through (0, 90), (2, 80), (4, 70), (6, 60), (8, 50), (10, 40), and (12, 30).

explanation: Find the graphed line's equation. It starts at 90 and falls 10 cases every 2 weeks, so its slope is $-5$ and the line is $y = 90 - 5x$. Set the two equal: $90 - 5x = 3x + 42$. Then $48 = 8x$, so $x = 6$. The question asks for $y$: $y = 3(6) + 42 = 60$. Check: $90 - 5(6) = 60$.

common_errors.why: Entered the week $x$ instead of the number of cases $y$.
Read County A's vertical intercept, which is not on County B's line.
Took the constant in County B's equation as the answer.

stem: The graph shows the percent $y$ of fern spores among all the plant microfossils in a sediment core, at depth $d$ meters. For conifer pollen, $y = 64 - 2d$. If $(d, y)$ is the solution to the system of the graphed line and the conifer equation, what is $d$?
stimulus: A paleobotanist counts plant microfossils in a lake-bed core. Fern spores become more common deeper in the core, and conifer pollen becomes less common.

figure.caption: Fern Spores by Core Depth
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 4), (2, 12), (4, 20), (6, 28), (8, 36), (10, 44), and (12, 52).

explanation: Read the fern line's equation from the graph. It crosses the vertical axis at 4 and rises 8 percentage points every 2 meters, so its slope is 4 and the line is $y = 4d + 4$. Set the two equal: $4d + 4 = 64 - 2d$. Add $2d$ and subtract 4 to get $6d = 60$, so $d = 10$. Check: $4(10) + 4 = 44$ and $64 - 2(10) = 44$.

common_errors.why: Entered the shared percent $y$ instead of the depth $d$, which swaps the coordinates.
Read the fern line's vertical intercept, a point on only one line.
Took the constant in the conifer equation as the answer.
Subtracted $2d$ from both sides instead of adding it: $2d = 60$, so $d = 30$.

stem: The graph shows the distance $y$, in thousands of kilometers, between Probe A and a moon $t$ hours after tracking began. Probe B's distance is $y = 120 - 10t$. If $(t, y)$ is the solution to the system of the graphed line and Probe B's equation, what is $t + y$?
stimulus: Astronomers are tracking two probes near the same moon. Probe A is drifting away from it, and Probe B is closing in for a landing.

figure.caption: Probe A Distance from Moon
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 15), (2, 25), (4, 35), (6, 45), (8, 55), (10, 65), and (12, 75).

explanation: Read Probe A's equation from the graph. It starts at 15 and rises 10 thousand km every 2 hours, so its slope is 5 and the line is $y = 5t + 15$. Set the two equal: $5t + 15 = 120 - 10t$. Then $15t = 105$, so $t = 7$, and $y = 5(7) + 15 = 50$. Check: $120 - 10(7) = 50$. The question asks for the sum: $7 + 50 = 57$.

common_errors.why: Found $t$ and stopped before working out $y$ and adding.
Found the solution but entered $y$ alone instead of $t + y$.
Used Probe A's vertical intercept $(0, 15)$, a point on only the graphed line, and added its coordinates.
Used Probe B's starting point $(0, 120)$ from its equation as the solution, giving $0 + 120$.

stem: The graph shows Rosa's weekly pay $y$, in dollars, at Job A for $x$ hours of work, which includes a fixed stipend. At Job B, $y = 17x$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system of the graphed line and Job B's equation, what is the value of $x$?
stimulus: A labor economist studies how part-time workers choose between two jobs. Job A pays an hourly wage plus a fixed weekly stipend. Job B pays a higher hourly wage and no stipend.

figure.caption: Job A Weekly Pay
figure.alt: A straight increasing line passing through (0, 60), (5, 120), (10, 180), (15, 240), and (20, 300).

explanation: Read Job A's equation from the graph. It crosses the vertical axis at 60 and rises \$60 every 5 hours, so its slope is 12 and the line is $y = 12x + 60$. Set the two equal: $12x + 60 = 17x$. Subtract $12x$ to get $60 = 5x$, so $x = 12$. Check: $12(12) + 60 = 204$ and $17(12) = 204$.

common_errors.why: Entered the shared weekly pay $y$ instead of the hours $x$.
Read Job A's vertical intercept, the stipend, which is a point on only one line.
Stopped at $5x = 60$ and took the coefficient 5 as the answer instead of dividing.

stem: The graph shows the water level $y$, in meters, in Reservoir P, $x$ hours after a spillway gate opened. Reservoir Q's level is $y = x + 8$. If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system of the graphed line and Reservoir Q's equation, what is the value of $y$?
stimulus: During a dam inspection, civil engineers lower Reservoir P through a spillway into the basin of Reservoir Q, so Q fills as P drains.

figure.caption: Reservoir P Water Level
figure.alt: A straight decreasing line passing through (0, 36), (2, 30), (4, 24), (6, 18), (8, 12), (10, 6), and (12, 0).

explanation: Find Reservoir P's equation from the graph. It starts at 36 m and falls 6 m every 2 hours, so its slope is $-3$ and the line is $y = 36 - 3x$. Set the two equal: $36 - 3x = x + 8$. Then $28 = 4x$, so $x = 7$. The question asks for $y$: $y = 7 + 8 = 15$. Check: $36 - 3(7) = 15$.

common_errors.why: Entered the time $x$ instead of the water level $y$.
Read Reservoir P's starting level, its vertical intercept, which is not on Q's line.
Took the constant in Reservoir Q's equation as the answer.
Combined $-3x$ and $-x$ as $-2x$: $2x = 28$, so $x = 14$ and $y = 14 + 8 = 22$.
